questions.stem: The soft yellow plaques deposited on the medial eyelid skin of this patient are most characteristic of which lipid abnormality?

explanation.summary: Xanthelasma are lipid-laden macrophage deposits in the periorbital skin and are a cutaneous marker of dyslipidemia, especially elevated LDL cholesterol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Xanthelasma are lipid-laden macrophage deposits in the periorbital skin and are a cutaneous marker of dyslipidemia, especially elevated LDL cholesterol.

questions.stem: The arrow points to a gray-white ring at the periphery of the cornea in this patient with dyslipidemia. What is this finding?

explanation.summary: Corneal arcus is a ring of lipid deposition at the corneal margin; when present in younger patients it suggests underlying hyperlipidemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Corneal arcus is a ring of lipid deposition at the corneal margin; when present in younger patients it suggests underlying hyperlipidemia.

questions.stem: In this lipoprotein metabolism diagram, the molecule labeled PCSK9 is shown acting at the hepatic LDL receptor. What is PCSK9's effect there?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It activates LDL receptors to clear more LDL

choices.label: C
choices.text: It promotes degradation of LDL receptors, raising plasma LDL

choices.label: E
choices.text: It converts VLDL directly into chylomicrons

explanation.summary: PCSK9 binds hepatic LDL receptors and targets them for lysosomal degradation, reducing LDL clearance and raising plasma LDL; its inhibition is a therapeutic strategy for hypercholesterolemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: PCSK9 binds hepatic LDL receptors and targets them for lysosomal degradation, reducing LDL clearance and raising plasma LDL; its inhibition is a therapeutic strategy for hypercholesterolemia.
